At 0<t<1 the squared generalized-binomial series has positive coefficients, proving I′_p>0; the reverse covariance of X and X^(p/2-1) bounds B_p>=I_p/(1+t²). Differentiation yields I′_p<=pt I_p/(1+t²), hence J_p=(p+1)I_p-(t+1)I′_p>0. At t=1 differentiability follows from integrability |theta-pi|^p, and t>1 follows from I_p(t)=t^p I_p(1/t) and the strict bound t>p. For every inclusion, the linear center/radius interpolation obeys |dc/dr|<=1; its weighted-perimeter derivative is bounded below by r^p(R-r)J_p>0. p=0 is perimeter, p>=1 comes from the credited published convex ridge theorem. For -1<p<0, near t=1-δ, the positive part of I′_p grows at least like δ^p while negative part is uniformly integrable, so J_p<0 for sufficiently small δ; the inward center shift with radius enlargement yields proper nested counterexamples both containing 0. An independent bounded script checked 32 positive slope settings and four representative negative cases; its initial p=-0.1 at finite δ did not cross into the asymptotic negative regime, and was correctly not used to invalidate or prove the quantifier. The analytical singular argument supplies universal negative p cases.

originality.rationale: PASS on the compared published full primary sources, with a specific missing 2026 full-text risk. Resultary Nov8 exact disk convex-ridge result explicitly proves p>=1 and leaves the fractional 0<p<1 range open. Saracco–Stefani Theorem 1.1, read in published full text, concerns all convex-body shapes, whose only universally monotone isotropic weights are constants; it is not a disk-only theorem. Csató–Giovagnoli 2026 restricts its monotonicity to origin-contained bodies, while the new statement handles arbitrarily translated disks including those missing origin. Fixed-center translated sphere formula cannot compare moving centers. A 2026 pth-moments shape optimization preprint treats perimeter-constrained extrema rather than nested inclusion. No exact fractional-power disk implication was found; the inaccessible complete Csató manuscript remains a named risk.
residual_risks: The full 2026 Csató–Giovagnoli manuscript and the newly updated 2608.19851 pth-moment preprint were not read in full; a differently stated disk-specialized inequality might affect priority.
The p>=1 range is prior published work, explicitly used rather than claimed as newly proved.
The negative-power singular behavior requires taking a p-dependent sufficiently small gap δ; a single finite-δ numerical counterexample does not cover all -1<p<0.

final_claim: For any two positive-radius nested planar Euclidean disks and exponent p>-1, the boundary integral of ||x||^p is inclusion-monotone for every pair exactly when p>=0; it is strictly increasing under proper inclusion for p>=0. Every -1<p<0 admits an explicit properly nested inward-shift counterexample with both disks containing the origin.
limitations: Restricted to full-dimensional planar disks and p>-1 (integrability at an origin-crossing circle); does not claim fractional monotonicity for arbitrary convex bodies or all radial weights.
